lines.dialogue: Cancer of the jaw.
No notes. No prior sign. Each of them in a strange location that means nothing to them where they’ve never gone before... That’s not how I’d kill myself.
How fresh? 13. MISS. HOOPER Just in. 67, natural causes. Used to work here, donated his body. I knew him. He was nice.
Fine. We’ll start with the riding crop. CUT TO: MISS. HOOPER So. Bad day, was it?
I need to know what bruises form in the next twenty minutes. Text me. MISS. HOOPER Listen, I was wondering, maybe later, when you’re finished --
Are you wearing lipstick? You weren’t wearing lipstick before. MISS. HOOPER I just ... refreshed it a bit.
Sorry, you were saying? MISS. HOOPER I was wondering if you’d like to have coffee?
Black, two sugars, please I’ll be upstairs. 14. 14A. MISS. HOOPER ... okay.
Mike, can I borrow your phone? No signal on mine.
I’d rather text.
Oh, thank you.
Afghanistan or Iraq?
Which was it? Afghanistan or Iraq?
Coffee! Thank you, Molly! What happened to the lipstick? MISS. HOOPER It ... wasn’t working for me.
Really? I thought it was a big improvement - mouth’s too small now. MISS. HOOPER ... okay.
How do you feel about the violin?
I play the violin when I’m thinking, and sometimes I don’t talk for days on end - would that bother you? Potential flatmates should know the worst about each other.

I did. I said to Mike this morning, that I was a difficult man to find a flatmate for. Now he turns up after lunch with an old friend clearly just home from military service in Afghanistan. Wasn’t a difficult leap.

I’ve got my eye on a nice little place in central London - together we could afford it. We’ll meet there, tomorrow evening, 7 o’clock. Sorry, got to dash - I think I left my riding crop in the mortuary.
Is that what?
Problem?
I know you’re an army doctor and you’ve been invalided home from Afghanistan. 17.

I know you’ve got a brother with a bit of money who’s worried about you, but you won’t go to him for help because you don’t approve of him - possibly because he’s an alcoholic, more likely because he recently walked out on his wife. And I know that your therapist thinks your limp is psychosomatic - quite correctly, I’m afraid. That’s enough to be going on with, don’t you think?
The name’s Sherlock Holmes and the address is 221b Baker Street. Afternoon.
Hi.
Sherlock, please.
Mrs. Hudson, the landlady. She’s giving me a special deal. Owes me a favour - few years ago, her husband got himself sentenced to death in Florida. I was able to help out.
Oh, no. I ensured it. 20. MRS. HUDSON Sherlock! CUT TO:
Yes, I think so. My thoughts exactly. JOHN SHERLOCK
Obviously I can straighten things up a bit.
Friend of mine. Well I say friend ... MRS. HUDSON What do you think, Dr. Watson - there’s another bedroom upstairs. If you’ll be needing two bedrooms ... 21.
Anything interesting?
What did you think?
Yes. And I can read your military career in your face and your leg, and the drinking habits of your brother in your mobile phone.
Four. There’s been a fourth. And there’s something different this time. 22. MRS. HUDSON A fourth? How do you know?
Where?
What’s different about this one. You wouldn’t have come to get me, if there wasn’t something new.
Yeah.
... Who’s on Forensics?
Anderson won’t work with me.
But I need an assistant.
Not in a police car. I’ll be right behind you.
Brilliant!

And I thought it was going to be a boring evening. Serial suicides, and now a note - oh, it’s Christmas! Mrs. Hudson, I’ll be late - might need some food. MRS. HUDSON I’m your landlady, dear, not your housekeeper.

Something cold is fine. John make yourself at home - have a cuppa! Don’t wait up! MRS. HUDSON Oh, look at him, dashing about? My husband was just the same. MRS. HUDSON But you’re more the sitting down type, I can tell. I’ll make you that cuppa, you rest your leg.
You’re a doctor.
In fact, you’re an army doctor.
Any good?
Seen a lot of injuries then. Violent deaths? 25.
Bit of trouble too, I bet.
Want to see some more?
Get your coat. CUT TO:
Impossible suicides - four of them. No point in sitting at home when there’s finally something fun going on! MRS. HUDSON Look at you, all happy. It’s not decent. 26.
Who cares about decent. The game, Mrs. Hudson, is on! CUT TO:
Taxi! CUT TO:
Okay, you’ve got questions!
Crime scene, next.
What do you think?
But?
I’m a consulting detective. Only one in the world, I invented the job.
It means when the police are out of their depth - which is always - they consult me.
When I first met you yesterday I said, Afghanistan or Iraq? You seemed surprised.
I didn’t know. I saw.
Tanned face --
-- but no tan above the wrists. You’ve been abroad but not sunbathing.
Your haircut and the way you hold yourself says military - but your conversation as you entered the room -- 28.
-- says you trained at Barts. So - army doctor. Obvious!

Your limp is really bad when you walk, but you don’t ask for a chair when you stand, like you’ve forgotten about it - so it’s at least partly psychosomatic. That says the circumstances of the original injury were traumatising - wounded in action then.
Wounded in action, a suntan. Afghanistan or Iraq?
You’ve got psychosomatic limp, of course you’ve got a therapist. Then there’s your brother --
Your phone. Expensive, email enabled, mp3 player - you’re looking for a flatshare, you wouldn’t waste money on this. It’s a gift then.
Scratches - not just one, but many over time. Been in the same pocket as keys and coins. 29.
The man in front of me wouldn’t treat his one luxury item like this, so there’s been a previous owner. Next bit’s easy - you know it already.

Harry Watson - clearly a family member who’s given you his old phone. Not your father - this is a young man’s gadget. Could be a cousin, but you’re a war hero who can’t find a place to live - unlikely you’ve got an extended family, certainly not one you’re close to. So - brother it is.
Now Clara, who’s Clara - three kisses says it’s a romantic attachment, the expense of the phone says wife not girlfriend.

She must have given it to him recently, this model’s only six months old. It’s a marriage in trouble then - six months on he’s just given it away. If she’d left him, he’d probably have kept the phone - people do, sentiment - but no, he wanted rid of it: he left her. He gave the phone to you - that says he wants you to stay in touch. 30.
You’re looking for cheap accommodation, but you’re not going to your brother for help - that says you’ve got problems with him. Maybe you liked his wife, maybe you don’t like his drinking --
Shot in the dark - good one though. The power connection.
Tiny little scuff marks all round it - he plugs it in every night to recharge, but his hands are shaking. Never see those marks on a sober man’s phone, never see a drunk’s without them.
There you go, you see? You were right.
The police don’t consult amateurs.
Do you think so?
That’s not what people usually say.
Piss off. CUT TO:
Did I get anything wrong?
Spot on, then! Didn’t expect to be right about everything.
... Harry’s your sister.
Your sister.
There’s always something! 32.
I’m here to see Detective Inspector Lestrade.
I was invited.
I think he wants me to take a look.
Always, Sally. I even know you didn’t make it home last night.
Colleague of mine, Dr. Watson. Dr. Watson - Sergeant Sally Donovan. Old friend.
No!
Anderson! Here we are again.
And is your wife away for long?
Your deoderant told me that.
It’s for men --
So’s Seargent Donovan.
Oh! And I think it just vapourised! May I go in?
I’m not implying anything - I’m sure Sally just came round for a lovely little chat, and happened to stay over. And I assume scrubbed your floors, going by the state of her knees -- 34.
I may need longer. CUT TO:
You’ll need to put this on.
He’s with me.
I told you - he’s with me.
So where are we? 35A.
Shut up!
You were thinking. It’s annoying. 36. 36A. 37.
Not much.
Yes, thank you for your input.
Of course, she’s not German. She’s from out of town though. Planned to spend a single night in London, before returning home to Cardiff. So far, so obvious.
Dr. Watson, what do you think?
Of the body, you’re a medical man.
They won’t work with me.
Yeah. Cos you need me.
Dr. Watson!
Well?
Helping me make a point.
Yeah, this is more fun.
Perfectly sound analysis, but I was hoping you’d go deeper.
You know what it was, you’ve read the papers.

Victim is in her late forties. Professional person going by her clothes - I’d guess something in the media, going by the frankly alarming shade of pink. She’s travelled from Cardiff today, intending to stay for one night - that’s obvious from the size of her suitcase --
Suitcase, yes. She’s been married for at least ten years, but not happily. She’s had a string of lovers, but none of them have known she was married -- 40.

The wedding ring, ten years old at least. The rest of her jewellery has been regularly cleaned, but not her wedding rings - state of her marriage, right there. The inside of the rings are shinier than the outside - that means they’re regularly removed; the only polishing they get is when she works them off her finger. It’s not for work - look at her nails, she doesn’t work with her hands - so what, or rather who, does she remove her rings for? Clearly not one lover - she’d never sustain the fiction of being single over time - so more likely a string of them. Simple!
Obvious, isn’t it?
Dear God, what’s it like in your funny little brains, it must be so boring. Her coat!

It’s slightly damp - she’s been in heavy rain within the last few hours. No rain anywhere in London in that time. Under her coat collar is damp too. She turned it up against the wind! She’s got an umbrella in her left pocket but it’s unused and dry. Not just wind, strong wind - too strong to use her umbrella. 41.

We know from her suitcase that she’s staying over night so she must have a come a decent distance. But she can’t have travelled more than two or three hours, cos her coat hasn’t dried. So where has there been heavy rain and strong wind within the radius of that travel time? Cardiff.
Do you know you do that out loud?
No, it’s fine.
Yeah, where is it? She must have a phone or an organiser - we can find out who Rachel is.
No, she was leaving an angry note in German - of course she was writing Rachel. No other word it can be. Question is, why did she wait till she was dying to write it...

Back of her right leg. Tiny splashes on the heel and calf, not present on the left. She was dragging a wheeled suitcase behind her, with her right hand - you don’t get that splash pattern any other way. Smallish case, going by the spread. Case that size, woman this clothes-conscious - could only be an overnight bag. So we know she was staying one night. Now where is it - what have you done with it? 42.
... say that again.
Suitcase! Did anyone find a suitcase - was there a suitcase in this house.
But they take the poison themselves. They chew and swallow the pills themselves, there are clear signs - even you lot couldn’t miss them.
... it’s murder. All of them. I don’t know how, but they’re not suicides, they’re killings - serial killings. We’ve got a serial killer. Love those, there’s always something to look forward to.
Where’s her case? Come on, where is it? Did she eat it? Someone else was here - and they took the case. So the killer must have driven her here - forgot the case was in the car ...
She never made it to her hotel Look at her hair - colour co- ordinates her lipstick and her shoes, she’d never have left a hotel with her hair still like --
Oh! Oh!
Serial killers, always hard. You’ve got to wait for them to make a mistake ...
Oh, we’re done waiting. Look at her! Really, look! Houston, we have a mistake!
Get on to Cardiff, find Jennifer Wilson’s family and friends - find Rachel.-
Pink!! 44.
Nicotine patch, helps me think! Impossible to sustain a smoking habit in London these days - bad news for brain work!
Oh, breathing - breathing’s boring.
It’s a three patch problem.
Oh, yes, of course. Can I borrow your phone?
Don’t want to use mine - always a chance the number’ll be recognised. It’s on the website.
Yeah, but she’s downstairs. I tried shouting, she didn’t hear me.
There was no hurry.
Her case.
Her suitcase, yes, obviously! The murderer took her suitcase. The first big mistake.
... it’s no use. There’s no other way, we’ll have to risk it. There’s a phone number on my desk - I want you to send a text.
A text, yes! Number on the desk!
What’s wrong? 58.
A friend.
Oh! Which one?
... did he offer you money to spy on me?
Did you take it?
Pity. We could’ve split the fee. Think it through next time.
The most dangerous man you’ve ever met and not my problem, right now. On my desk, the number!
Yes, doesn’t matter, just enter the number. Are you doing it.
Have you done it? 59.
Now these words exactly. “What happened at Lauriston Gardens? I must have blacked out. Northumberland Street. Please come.”
What? No, no. Type and send, quickly.
Sent it yet?
22 Northumberland Street, hurry up!
Yes, of course it is. Oh, I should probably mention that I didn’t kill her.
Why not? Given the text I just had you send, and the fact I have this case, it would be a perfectly logical assumption. 60.
Now and then, yes.
By looking.

The killer must have driven her to Lauriston Gardens. He could only keep her case by accident, if it was in a car. No one could be seen with this case without attracting attention - particularly a man, which is statistically likely. So obviously he’d feel compelled to get rid of it the moment he noticed he still had it - wouldn’t have taken him more than five minutes to realise his mistake. CUT TO: 61.
I checked every back street wide enough for a car within five minutes of Lauriston Gardens and looked for anywhere you could dispose of a bulky object without being observed. CUT TO:
Took me less than an hour to find the right skip. CUT TO:
It had to be pink. Obviously.
Because you’re an idiot.
Don’t look like that - practically everyone is. Now look - do you see what’s missing?
Her phone. Where’s her mobile phone. No phone on the body, no phone in her case. We know she has one - the number’s right there, and you just texted it. 62.
She has a string of lovers, and she’s careful about it - she never leaves it at home.
The question is, where is that phone now?
Yes. Or?
Maybe she left it in his car, when she left her case. Maybe he took it for some other reason. Either way, the balance of probability is that the murderer has her phone.
A few hours since his last victim - and now he’s got a text which can only be from her ... Now someone who’d just found the phone would ignore a text like that. But the murderer -
-- would panic. 63.
Four people are dead - there isn’t time to talk to the police.
Mrs. Hudson took my skull.
Relax, you’re doing fine. Well?
Well you could just sit here and watch telly ...
I prefer company when I go out - I think better aloud, and the skull just attracts attention.
Problem?
What about her?
And I said “dangerous”. And here you are. 64.
Northumberland Street is five minutes walk from here.
No, I think he’s brilliant enough. I love the brilliant ones - they’re so desperate to get caught.
Appreciation! Applause!
At long last, the spotlight! That’s the frailty of genius, John - it needs an audience.
This is his hunting ground. Right here in the heart of the city. 65.

We now know the victims were abducted, and that changes everything. Because all of his victims disappeared from crowded places, from busy streets - but nobody saw them go. They walked out of their lives with a complete stranger, and trusted him right to the moment they swallowed his poison. He can do the impossible, this one - he needs to take a bow.
Yes. That’s odd. ‘Til we know who Rachel is, no point in speculating. Mustn’t theorise in advance of the facts.
Think, though, think! Who do we trust, even if don’t know them? Who passes unnoticed wherever they go? Who hunts in the middle of a crowd?
Haven’t the faintest. Hungry? CUT TO:
Thankyou, Billy 66.
22 Northumberland Street. Keep your eyes on it.
Well he has killed four people.
Do you want to eat?
This is Angelo. Three years ago I successfully proved to Lestrade that at the time of a particularly vicious triple-murder, Angelo was in a completely different part of town, house-breaking.
I cleared it a bit. Anything happening opposite?
Oh, he’s just drunk. photo) Also married with a dog.
Married with a dog. Keep your eyes peeled.
You did go to prison.
You may as well eat - we might have a long wait.
I’m sorry?
Doesn’t it? Sounds a bit dull.
What do real people have then? In their real lives?
Yes, well as I was saying - dull!
A girlfriend? No. Not really my area.
I know it’s fine.
... John, you should know, I consider myself married to my work, and while I’m flattered by your interest I’m really not looking for any kind of --
Good, thankyou.
Nothing in real life, apparently. Take a look across the street. 70.
In a taxi! That’s clever! Is it clever? Why’s that clever?
Don’t stare.
Well we can’t both stare. CUT TO:
Good for you.
Left turn, one way, roadworks, traffic lights, bus lane, pedestrian crossing, left turn only, traffic lights ... 71.
Police, pull over, now. Pull over!
Open up, come on, now! 74.
No! Teeth, tan, what, Californian? LA, Santa Monica, just arrived.
The luggage!
Oh, and your first trip to London probably - going by your destination, and the route this driver has taken you.
Yes. Is everything all right?
Welcome to London.
Basically.
No, not the murderer.
As they go. 75.
Yeah. I pick-pocket him when he’s annoying. You can keep that one, I’ve got loads at the flat.
What?
Got your breath back?
And you invaded Afghanistan.
Oh, they can keep an eye out. It’s a long shot anyway.
Passing the time, proving a point.
You.
Mrs. Hudson, Dr. Watson will be taking the upstairs room!
Says the man at the door.
Mrs. Hudson? MRS. HUDSON Upstairs! CUT TO:
What are you doing??
You can’t just break into my flat!
Well what do you call this??
John ...
John, you probably want to shut up now... 78.
What?
Shut up! I’m not your sniffer dog.
What’s he doing here? On a drugs bust?
Put them back.
It’s an experiment.
This is childish.
What, so you set up a pretend drugs bust, to bully me?
I’m clean.
I don’t even smoke!
... Who is she?
Her daughter. Why would she write her daughter’s name, why?
I’m not a psychopath, Anderson - I’m a high-functioning sociopath. Do your research! You need to bring Rachel in, you need to question her. I need to question her -
Excellent! How? When? Is there a connection? There has to be! 80.
No. No, that’s not right. Why would she do that?
She didn’t think about her daughter, she scratched her name on the floor. She was dying, it took effort, it would’ve hurt - she was trying to tell us something!
Oh, but that was ages ago - why would she still be upset?
Not good?
Yes, but listen! If you were dying, if you’d been murdered, in your very last seconds, what would you say.
Oh, use your imagination!

Yes, but if you were clever, if you were very clever... Jennifer Wilson, running all those lovers. She was clever, and she’s telling us something! 81. MRS. HUDSON Isn’t the doorbell working? Your taxi’s here, Sherlock.
I didn’t order a taxi, go away. MRS. HUDSON Oh dear, they’re making such a mess. What are they looking for?
Shut up! Everybody shut up, I’m thinking, don’t move, don’t breathe, Anderson, face the other way, you’re putting me off!
Come on, come on!! MRS. HUDSON What about your taxi -
Mrs. Hudson!! 82.

Oh, she was clever. Clever, yes, I love her! She’s cleverer than you lot dead! Do you see? Do you get it? She didn’t lose her phone, she never lost it. She planted in on him. When she got out that car, she knew she was going to her death - she left the phone to lead us to her killer!
What do you mean, how? Rachel, don’t you see? Rachel!! Oh, look at you lot, you’re all so vacant! What’s it like, not being me, it must be so relaxing. Rachel is not a name.
John, the luggage label, it had an email address on it.
I’ve been too slow, she didn’t have a laptop, which means did her business on her phone. So it’s a smartphone, it’s email enabled. So there’s a website for her account.
The user name will be the email address -
- and all together now, the password is ... ? 83.
Don’t talk out loud, Anderson, you lower the IQ of the whole street. We can do more than read her emails - it’s a smartphone, it’s got GPS. And if you lose it ...
... you can locate it online.
She’s leading us right to the man who killed her.
computer Come on, quickly, quickly! MRS. HUDSON Sherlock, dear this taxi driver!
Mrs. Hudson, isn’t it time for your evening soother?
Get some vehicles ready, get a helicopter, we need to move fast - that phone battery won’t last forever.
It’s a start!
It narrows it down from anyone in London, it’s the first proper lead we’ve had.
Where is it, where, quickly!
But it can’t be. How can it be here? How??
And I didn’t notice. Me?? I didn’t notice.
Who do we trust, even if don’t know them?
Who passes unnoticed wherever they go?
Who hunts in the middle of a crowd? 86.
What? Yes, yes.
I don’t know ...
Good idea.
Nowhere. Fresh air, just popping out for a moment.
I’m fine! CUT TO: 87.
I didn’t order a taxi.
You’re the cabbie - the one who stopped outside Northumberland Street. It was you, not your passenger.
Is this a confession?
Why?
Am I not?
No one else will die though. I believe they call that a result. 88.
If I wanted to understand ... what would I do?
So you can kill me too?
How did you find me? 90A.
Who would warn you about me?
... who?
Who would notice me?
I’m really not.
Tell me more.
Where are we? 92.
Roland-Kerr further education college. Why here?
And you just walk your victims in? How?
Oh, dull!
You can’t make people kill themselves at gunpoint.
No, I’m not.
Bit of a risk, wasn’t it? You took me away under the noses of about half a dozen policemen - they’re not that stupid. And Mrs. Hudson will remember you.
Love what?
My fan?
Oh, I see. So you’re a proper genius too.
Okay, two bottles. Explain.
The bottles are, of course, identical.
And you know which is which.
But I don’t.
Why should I? I’ve got nothing to go on! What’s in it for me?
This is what you did? To all of them? You gave them a choice?
That isn’t a game - it’s chance.
Play what? It’s a 50-50 chance.
It’s still chance.
It’s luck.
Either way, you’re wasted as a cabbie. CUT TO: CUT TO: 98.
You risked your life four times ... just to kill strangers? Why?
I am playing. This is my go. There’s shaving foam behind your ear, and no one’s pointed it to you.
There are traces where it’s happened before, so clearly you live alone - there’s no one to tell you.

But you have photographs of children. The children’s mother has been cut out the photograph - if she’d died, she’d still be there. The photograph is old, but the frame is new. You think of your children, but you don’t get to see them. Estranged father, she took the kids, but you still love them, and it still hurts.

Oh, but there’s more! Your clothes are freshly laundered, but everything you’re wearing is at least three years old. Keeping up appearances, but not planning ahead. And here you are, on a kamikaze murder spree, what’s that about? Ah! Three years ago, is that when they told you?
That you’re a dead man walking.
You don’t have long. Am I right?
And because you’re dying, you’ve just murdered four people.
No. No, there’s something else. You haven’t killed four people because you’re bitter. Bitterness is a paralytic - love is a much more vicious motivator. Somehow, this is about your children.
But how?
Or serial killing. 100.
Surprise me.
You have a what?
Who would sponsor a serial killer?
Who.
What do you mean, more? Who is he? Tell me!
What if I don’t take either? I could walk away from this table right now.
I’ll have the gun please.
Definitely. The gun.
The gun.
I know a real gun when I see one.
Clearly. This has been most interesting. I look forward to your court case. 102.
Of course. Childs play.
Was I right? I was, wasn’t I? Did I get it right?
Ok then. Tell me this. Your sponsor - who is it? 105A.
The one who told you about me. My fan. I want a name.
You’re dying, but there’s still time to hurt you. Give me a name.
A name! Now!
Name him!!
Why do I have this blanket? They keep putting a blanket on me.
I’m not in shock!
So, the shooter. No sign of him.
Oh, I wouldn’t say that ...

The bullet they just dug out the wall was from a hand gun. A kill shot over that distance from that kind of weapon - that’s a crack shot you’re looking for. But not just a marksmen, a fighter - his hand couldn’t have shaken at all, so clearly he’s acclimatised to violence. He didn’t fire ‘til I was in immediate danger, though. So, strong moral principles. You’re looking for a man probably with a history of military service and nerves of steel --
Actually, you know what - ignore me.
Ignore all that. It’s the shock talking! 107.

Just need to ... discuss the rent. LESTRADE Still got questions for you. SHERLOCK What, now? I’m in shock. Look, I’ve got a blanket. LESTRADE Sherlock ... SHERLOCK And I did just catch a serial killer for you. More or less. LESTRADE ... Okay. We’ll pull you in tomorrow - off you go.
them) Good shot.
Well you’d know.
We’ll need to get the powder burns out your finger. I don’t suppose you’d serve time for this, but let’s avoid the court case. Are you all right?
You have just killed a man. 108.
No. No, he wasn’t really, was he?
Yeah, that’s true. A very bad cabbie. You should’ve seen the route we took here. 108A.
Don’t blame me. You shot him!
Sorry.
Course I wasn’t. Playing for time. Knew you’d show up.
Why would I do that?
Dinner?
There’s a good Chinese, end of Baker Street - stays open ‘til two. You can always tell a good Chinese by examining the bottom third of the doorhandle -- 110.
I know exactly who that is. M So! Another case cracked. How very public spirited of you. Though that’s never really ever your motivation, is it?
What are you doing here? M As ever ... I am concerned about you.
Yes. I’ve been hearing about your concern. 111. M Always so aggressive. Does it never occur to you that you and I belong on the same side.
Oddly enough, no. M We have more in common than you like to believe. This petty feud between us - it’s simply childish. People will suffer. And you know how it always upset Mummy.
I upset her? Me? It wasn’t me who upset her, Mycroft -
Mother. Our Mother. This is my brother, Mycroft. Are you putting on weight? M Losing it, in fact.
Of course he’s my brother.
Not what?
Close enough. M Oh for goodness sake! I occupy a minor post in the British Government. 112.

He is the British Government. When he’s not too busy being the British Secret Service. And the CIA on a freelance basis. Good evening, Mycroft - try not to start a war before I get home, you know what it does to the traffic.
I can always predict the fortune cookies.
I nearly can. You did get shot though?
In Afghanistan. There was an actual wound.
The shoulder. I thought so.
The left one.
I never guess.
Moriarty.
I have absolutely no idea.
Hey. 7.
You took your time.
What? Why not?
You had a row with a machine?
Take my card.
Not interested. I sent them a message. 8.
Of course.
Mine is in the bedroom. 8A.
In a manner of speaking. Took me less than a minute to guess yours. Not exactly Fort Knox.
There are forty-three.
Types of password. That people like you commonly use.
Ordinary.
There’s no point.
I see you’ve started a blog...
‘Imperious’. Not a word I’ve ever been called before. 9.
